dimensions.assessment: Involves federal officials at the GAO, SEC, and FINRA, as well as small- and medium-sized businesses undertaking IPOs.
dimensions.evidence: The Comptroller General of the United States, in consultation with the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority

dimensions.assessment: Mandates a research study and congressional report on financial and legal costs.
dimensions.evidence: carry out a study of the costs associated with small- and medium-sized companies to undertake initial public offerings

dimensions.assessment: No specific funding or budgetary figures are provided.
Directs a specific federal study and report without establishing new regulatory programs.
dimensions.evidence: issue a report to the Congress containing all findings and determinations

dimensions.assessment: One-time study with a 360-day deadline for completion.
dimensions.evidence: Not later than the end of the 360-day period beginning on the date of the enactment of this Act

missing_information: Cost of conducting the GAO study
importance_detail.rationale: Requires the Government Accountability Office to conduct a one-time study and report on initial public offering costs for small- and medium-sized companies.
